questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A pool fills at a constant rate. At 2 p.m. it holds 1,500 gallons; at 5 p.m. it holds 3,300 gallons. What is the rate, and how much water was in it at noon?
questions.prompt_markup:
A pool fills at a constant rate. At 2 p.m. it holds 1,500 gallons; at 5 p.m. it holds 3,300 gallons.
What is the rate, and how much water was in it at noon?
questions.correct_answer: 600 gallons per hour; 300 gallons at noon
questions.grading_note: Form required: the rate with units and the amount. 1,800 ÷ 3 = 600, and 1,500 - 2(600) = 300.

A taxi charges the same amount for every mile.

questions.correct_answer: Each mile adds the same amount, so the fare grows by equal differences over equal intervals, which is linear growth.
